## Abstract {.unnumbered}

Accurate progesterone receptor (PR) status is a critical determinant
of endocrine therapy eligibility in breast cancer. Although
immunohistochemistry (IHC) remains the clinical standard,
diagnostically ambiguous cases can exhibit substantial
inter-pathologist variability. Pathology images alone often lack
the molecular context needed to resolve these challenging receptor
states, while conventional late-fusion multimodal models struggle
to align transcriptomic information with localized histopathologic
features.

To address this challenge, we present a multimodal architecture
integrating RNA-Seq transcriptomic profiles with whole-slide
imaging. Our asymmetric cross-attention architecture enables each
patient's transcriptomic profile to guide visual evidence retrieval
directly from tissue images before slide-level aggregation while
preserving linear computational complexity. A Cross-Modal
Reliability Estimator produces per-patient confidence scores that
illustrate a potential mechanism for flagging ambiguous cases for
pathologist review. We additionally introduce a
normalization-corrected Top-1%-Mass Concentration metric that
quantifies attention localization consistently across slides of
varying size. In an exploratory survival analysis, a Cox model
combining the fusion architecture with the reliability signal
showed a higher point-estimate concordance index than clinical-only
and unimodal baselines, though the small event count limited
statistical power.

Using the TCGA-BRCA cohort of 951 patients, the model achieved an
ROC-AUC of **0.8482** and a PR-AUC of **0.9054**. Attention
patterns revealed significant phenotypic separation between
PR-positive and PR-negative tumors (*p* = 0.018), indicating that
the model captures biologically meaningful spatial patterns
associated with receptor status.

---

## Key Contributions & Findings {.unnumbered}

::: {.contributions}

- **Asymmetric Cross-Attention Architecture**
  Transcriptomic embeddings guide visual evidence retrieval before
  slide-level aggregation with **O(N)** computational complexity,
  improving ROC-AUC by **+0.0801** over late-fusion baselines.

- **Cross-Modal Reliability Signal**
A Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator produces per-patient
confidence scores, illustrating a potential mechanism for flagging uncertain predictions for pathologist review.

- **Size-Invariant Interpretability**
  A normalization-corrected attention concentration metric removes
  slide-size bias, revealing significant phenotype-specific
  attention patterns (*p* = 0.018) that entropy-based analysis
  fails to detect (*p* = 0.401).

:::

---

## Design Decisions {.unnumbered}

::: {.contributions}

- **Asymmetric over Bidirectional Attention.**
  Prioritized computational efficiency and scalability over
  modeling reciprocal cross-modal interactions, which are less
  critical for transcriptomics-guided evidence retrieval.

- **Upstream Fusion over Late Fusion.**
  Prioritized preserving localized morphological information by
  conditioning visual feature selection before slide-level
  aggregation, accepting increased architectural complexity.

- **Clinical Reliability over Maximum Discrimination.**
  Prioritized calibrated confidence estimation to support
  identification of ambiguous cases rather than optimizing predictive
  performance alone.

:::

---

## Limitations {.unnumbered}

::: {.contributions}

- **Single-Cohort Validation.**
  Trained and evaluated on TCGA-BRCA; performance across
  independent institutions, staining protocols, and acquisition
  platforms remains to be established.

- **Assay Availability.**
  Requires matched whole-transcriptome RNA-Seq data, which
  currently involves greater cost and turnaround time than
  standard IHC workflows.

- **Vision Encoder Alignment.**
  The current vision encoder was pretrained on pathology images
  alone, limiting cross-modal reliability. Joint multimodal
  pretraining or transcriptomics-guided visual representation
  learning represent promising directions for improving
  multimodal alignment.

:::

## Architecture {.unnumbered}

<img src="reports/figures/architecture.svg"
alt="System architecture diagram"/>

<p class="arch-caption">
System architecture. The transcriptomic stream produces a single
query token <em>Q</em> that attends over all <em>N</em> visual patch
embeddings with linear computational complexity. Predictions with
confidence below the calibrated threshold (<em>α</em> &lt; 0.75) would
be flagged for pathologist review in a deployed setting.
</p>
